newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Busang gold saga nears moment of truth.
newsitem.headline: Busang gold saga nears moment of truth.

text.p: The world mining community is waiting with bated breath for results next month that may show whether a controversial discovery deep in the Borneo jungle is the biggest gold strike this century or an elaborate hoax.

At the heart of the controversy is Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd, which went from penny-stock exploration firm to darling of the Toronto Stock Exchange, only to come crashing down when doubts emerged over how much golf is at the Busang property.
"There are two possibilities. There is either a gold mining project...or there isn't," said Simatupang, vice-chairman of the Indonesia Mining Association.
"If there is no gold there, Indonesia and the mining industry will indeed suffer a loss," he told Reuters "But at this point in time, we will have to wait for the results."

An independent audit being carried out under tight security by Canadian consulting company Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd to determine the size of the deposit might provide answers. The results are expected in early May.
Bre-X stunned the world last month when it said there was a strong possibility that the potential gold resources on the Busang property might have been overstated.
The company had previously estimated that Busang contained some 70.95 million ounces of gold worth $25 billion, making it the biggest find this century.
The announcement came just one week after Bre-X geologist Michael de Guzman mysteriously fell from a helicopter on the way to the Busang deposit he had helped discover on Borneo Island.

Indonesian officials had said de Guzman might have committed suicide because a letter left behind in the helicopter said he had been suffering from acute hepatitis. But his brother said de Guzman was not the kind of a person who might kill himself.

Earlier twists to the Busang saga included the failure of Barrick Gold Corp of Canada to get part of the property even though it was the front-runner, and failed attempts by President Suharto's children to be involved in the project.
In a surprising turn of events, U.S. mining giant Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc was picked as the sole mine operator after influential Indonesian tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan entered the scene.

Bre-X owns 45-percent of the Busang property, Freeport has 15 percent and the Indonesian government 10 percent. The Nusamba Group, 80-percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto, and its 50-percent partner own the remaining 30 percent.
Hasan, who heads Nusamba, and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto each have a 10-percent stake in Nusamba.
Industry officials said the shareholding in the Busang property would remain intact if the size of the gold deposit matched previous estimates by Bre-X.
"If the gold deposit is small, then I think Freeport will pull out because it would not be worth the while of a company like Freeport," one industry source said.
He said a mine could still be developed at Busang if the deposit was just one million ounces, adding that mines had been developed in Indonesia where gold deposits were no larger.
Since losing almost $2.2 billion of its stockmarket value last month, Bre-X shares have traded on the wildest of rumours while investors await Srathcona's audit.
One Indonesian industry official said a laboratory in Perth had completed assaying drilling samples obtained by Strathcona from Busang and that the results were being kept in a safe.

"The lab in Perth has completed the assaying and has locked it away in a safe," he said, adding the samples from the test drillings have also been sent to a laboratory in Indonesia's Balikpapan town in East Kalimantan and another in Canada.
"There has been no indication of the results and we are as anxious to know as you are," he said. "This whole thing has been so bizarre...one of the most bizarre things I have ever seen."
